themes.title: Far-right push for 'national priority' policies
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right parties across Europe are intensifying their advocacy for 'national priority' policies, which prioritize citizens over immigrants in access to social benefits, housing, and public services. This theme has gained traction in Spain, Italy, Sweden, and Norway, with parties like Vox, Fratelli d'Italia, Sverigedemokraterna, and Fremskrittspartiet leading the charge. The framing often ties these policies to broader anti-immigration rhetoric and critiques of multiculturalism.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox registers initiatives to ban public Islamic prayers and prioritize Spaniards in social housing and public aid, criticizing PP for allowing multicultural practices.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Lega and FdI support 'national priority' clauses in regional government agreements, such as in Castilla y León, to favor Italians in housing and social services.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: SD pushes for easing coastal protection laws to prioritize long-term residents over migrants, and advocates for stricter deportation rules for teenage migrants.

countries.name: 🇳🇴 Fremskrittspartiet
countries.note: FrP emphasizes traditional land use in Finnmark and opposes Sami consultations on snowmobile laws, framing it as a national priority issue.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: RN proposes halting immigration and reinstating mandatory minimum sentences to address post-PSG riot violence, framing it as a national security priority.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: AfD advocates for housing prioritization for long-term residents over asylum seekers in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, tying it to anti-immigration policies.

themes.title: Javier Milei’s declining approval amid internal strife
themes.blurb: Argentina's President Javier Milei continues to face declining approval ratings and internal conflicts within his La Libertad Avanza party. His government is grappling with economic challenges, judicial scandals involving key allies, and tensions with provincial governors. This theme resonates in Spain and Italy, where far-right parties like Vox and Fratelli d'Italia monitor Milei's trajectory as a potential model or cautionary tale for their own political strategies.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Milei's approval rating drops to 39.9% amid economic struggles, labor reforms, and scandals like Adorni's illicit enrichment allegations.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox closely watches Milei's struggles, with some leaders expressing concern over his economic policies and internal party conflicts as a cautionary tale.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump and his allies express mixed reactions to Milei's policies, with some praising his deregulation efforts and others criticizing his economic austerity measures.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian far-right parties debate Milei's approach to economic liberalization, with some viewing his policies as a potential model for Italy's fiscal reforms.

themes.title: Far-right gains in European local elections
themes.blurb: Far-right parties are making significant gains in local and regional elections across Europe, particularly in Germany, Italy, Spain, and Sweden. These victories reflect broader trends of rising far-right influence in national politics, often driven by anti-immigration sentiment, economic discontent, and dissatisfaction with mainstream parties. The theme highlights the growing normalization of far-right governance at the subnational level.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: AfD leads polls in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, with 36% support, and wins mayoral races in smaller towns like Görlitz.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: FdI and Lega secure victories in regional elections, such as in Liguria and Veneto, and form coalition governments with 'national priority' clauses.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox gains ground in Andalusia and Castilla y León, forming coalition governments with PP and pushing for anti-immigration policies.

countries.name: 🇸🇪 Sverigedemokraterna
countries.note: SD influences Sweden's migration policies, including raising the age limit for deporting teenage migrants and easing coastal protection laws.

themes.title: Internal divisions within far-right parties
themes.blurb: Far-right parties across Europe and the Americas are experiencing internal divisions, with factions clashing over leadership, policy direction, and electoral strategies. These conflicts often reflect broader ideological tensions between hardline and more moderate wings, as well as personal rivalries. The theme is evident in Poland, Hungary, the UK, France, and Argentina, where far-right parties struggle to maintain unity amid growing public scrutiny.

countries.name: 🇵🇱 Prawo i Sprawiedliwość
countries.note: PiS faces internal strife over leadership and cooperation with Konfederacja, with factions divided over electoral strategies and judicial appointments.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Tisza Party and Fidesz clash over constitutional amendments, EU funds, and the removal of President Tamás Sulyok, reflecting deep internal divisions.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: Reform UK struggles with leadership challenges, including Nigel Farage's exclusion from BBC's *Desert Island Discs* and internal debates over immigration policies.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: RN faces public splits between Jordan Bardella and Marine Le Pen over pension reforms and leadership succession ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Milei's government grapples with internal conflicts between factions led by Karina Milei and Santiago Caputo, particularly over judicial appointments and economic policies.

themes.title: Far-right reactions to Colombia’s presidential election
themes.blurb: Far-right parties and leaders in Argentina, Spain, the US, and Italy are reacting to the first-round victory of Colombia's far-right candidate, Abelardo de la Espriella. These reactions highlight transnational solidarity among far-right movements, with leaders like Javier Milei and Santiago Abascal congratulating de la Espriella and framing his victory as a rejection of socialism and a step toward freedom. The theme underscores the global interconnectedness of far-right political strategies.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Javier Milei congratulates de la Espriella, framing his victory as a rejection of socialism and a step toward freedom, aligning with Milei's own anti-socialist rhetoric.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Santiago Abascal celebrates de la Espriella's victory, calling it an opportunity for Colombia to reject socialism and embrace conservative values.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump and his allies express support for de la Espriella, viewing his victory as a sign of growing far-right influence in Latin America.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian far-right parties monitor de la Espriella's campaign, drawing parallels to their own anti-immigration and anti-socialist platforms.
